page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-128 is a large-scale general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor offering 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with symmetric multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 512 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, alongside AVX and BMI2 instruction sets. It lacks local storage and bundled GPU accelerators, requiring attached cloud block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high parallel compute capacity. In multi-threaded evaluations, the system delivers top-tier results, registering a score of 172,677.02 on stress-ng multi-core and 91,350.42 on PassMark CPU, bolstered by high throughput in physics simulations, ray tracing, and hardware-accelerated encryption. Single-core performance falls in the moderate to strong range, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,620.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2,711.68. The instance achieves strong performance in cached memory reads at 6,959.33 GB/s, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths measure at 146.02 GB/s and 67.88 GB/s respectively.

Given its high core count and aggregate RAM capacity, the instance offers strong cost efficiency for scale-up parallel compute workloads rather than single-threaded bottlenecks. Tradeoffs include the absence of integrated local NVMe disks and advanced vector instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX. The instance is suited for enterprise application backends, large-scale software compilation, batch processing pipelines, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and high-concurrency web serving environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-128 is a general-purpose instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs and 64 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 512 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance includes cryptographic acceleration instructions like AES and SHA-NI, but does not provide local storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-threaded compute efficiency, reaching 172,677.02 on stress-ng multi-core and 91,350.42 on PassMark CPU, alongside strong caching and ray tracing performance. Single-core performance remains moderate across Geekbench tests. Without local NVMe storage, persistent data relies entirely on network-attached volumes. This instance is suited for highly threaded enterprise workloads, large software builds, in-memory databases, and high-throughput static web serving.
